samir: Quick heads-up — ran a fused FlashAttention benchmark on an A100 cluster and hit intermittent NaNs/INF from the softmax path when using fp16. Repro (brief):
```
# run: python benchmarks/flash_attn_bench.py --batch 8 --seq 4096 --model gpt-like --dtype fp16 --kernel fused
```
Output: occasional lines like `softmax: inf` then GEMM overflows and output becomes NaN. Happens ~1/20 runs.

maria_g: Ugh, seen similar in fp8 experiments. Could be the softmax exponent blowing up before subtraction or accumulation in fp16 losing precision. Did you try bf16 or forcing fp32 accumulation?

samir: I did a quick diff: forcing bf16 via `TORCH_DEFAULT_DTYPE=bfloat16` removed the NaNs in my short run. Also forcing kernel `flash_attn_unfused` (non-fused) removes the problem. So looks like fused variant's reduction/accum path + fp16 = bad combo on A100.

devon: Interesting. Kernel selector right now picks `flash_attn_fused_v2` when seq_len > 2048 and batch small to maximize throughput. The selector heuristic is roughly: `if seq>2048 and gpu_mem>X and dtype==fp16 -> fused_v2`. Maybe we need an extra toggle for numerical risk. Any profiler output?

perf-bot: kernel=flash_attn_fused_v2; avg_ms=12.3; p50_ms=11.8; p95_ms=18.6; memory=28.1GB; run_id=20260315-21

kyra: Can you dump a NVTX/Profiler trace (nsys) + the kernel launch params? Also try enabling the numerically stable softmax variant (max-subtract) in fused kernel if present. On long sequences the exp range can overflow in fp16 quickly.

samir: Attached minimal log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15 21:07:12] flash_attn fused_v2 launch: grid=(1024,), block=(256,), smem=48KB
softmax forward: max=8.2, min=-2.1, sum: inf, found inf in output
cudaError: CUBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR
```
I also toggled GPU_ARCH flags; H100 didn't reproduce in my quick run (bf16 hardware support?)

maria_g: H100 has native bf16 and better fp16 accumulation paths, so that fits. For A100, maybe accumulation into fp32 in the fused kernel would help. But that'll hurt perf. We should add an automatic fallback: detect NaN/INF in softmax output and rerun that batch with higher precision / unfused kernel. That keeps perf most of the time and fixes tails.

devon: Agreed. Actionable plan: 1) Add a quick NVTX/trace to the fused kernel around softmax and an instrumented debug check that runs in CI only (detect inf/nan). 2) Update kernel selector: if dtype==fp16 and seq>3072 and trailing_token_distribution_skew>THRESH, prefer unfused or use accumulation_fp32 flag. 3) Add perf test to measure the regression for the fallback path. I'll open a PR.

samir: I can add a deterministic repro to `eng-runtime/tests/repro/` that triggers the failure (seeded inputs, long tail attention mask). Will include env vars and `--force-kernel` flag.

kyra: Also add an auto-fallback circuit in the serving runtime: detect batch-level NaN after generate step, mark that batch to rerun with fallback kernel and tag metric `attention.fallback.count`. That will help on prod.

maria_g: One more note: softmax stability trick: compute `y = exp(x - max(x))` in fp32 accumulation and then cast back. If we move accumulation to fp32 in the fused kernel for the softmax and only cast final results to fp16, we retain precision. We should benchmark cost.

devon: Yep. I'll prototype three variants and benchmark: (A) fused_fp16 (current), (B) fused_fp16_accum_fp32, (C) unfused_fp16. We'll run across seq [1024,2048,4096] and batch [1,8]. If (B) fixes correctness with <10% perf hit vs (A), we can enable it as selector option.

perf-bot: scheduled perf job: pr/attention-stability-2026 -> bench matrix start 2026-03-16 03:00 UTC; job_id=bench-5521

samir: For immediate prod safety: I'll add a short-circuit in the serving runtime to change model config `kernel_overflow_safety: true` which triggers auto-fallback for fp16 models with seq>2048. I'll post the repro and test cases in the PR.

maria_g: Also log the softmax max value per request (`attention.debug.max`) for a sample of requests so we can correlate with inputs that trigger it.

devon: I'll wire the selector change and add the perf tests. We'll also update the kernel metadata so the console shows recommended precision and warnings.

kyra: Sounds good. If someone can link the repro here after it's pushed I'll kick off an internal canary on dedicated infra. :thumbsup:

samir: Pushed repro branch `repro/attn-fp16-overflow-176328` with a README and seed. PR incoming.
